reason: E2 directly supports TiC formation and Ni solid solution bonding for a coated diamond/HEA system, but the hypothesis extrapolates this to a W–Cu system without direct evidence. E1 supports SPS for fine-grained, high-density consolidation but does not address coated powders or W–Cu. E3 is about 3D printing of MPEAs and is irrelevant to the key premises. The critical claims about TiC formation on W (not diamond) and Ni-mediated bonding with Cu are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Ti reacts with carbon to form a stable TiC layer during SPS
Ni in an outer layer can form a solid solution interface with a matrix
A Ti/Ni dual-layer coating can reduce voids and improve interfacial bonding in a composite
SPS can consolidate powders into a fine-grained, high-density material with controlled structure
The TiC/Ni interface will improve thermal conductivity and mechanical durability under irradiation
